rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Living, Self-Sustaining God repairs creatures' needs; that requires complete knowledge of them and power to meet them, supplied by 3:5 and 3:6 respectively.
rows.anchor: القائم بإصلاح مصالح الخلق ومهماتهم ، وكونه كذلك لا يتم إلا بمجموع أمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge cannot be established by transmitted testimony, since validating testimony already depends on knowing that God knows; reason must establish it.
rows.anchor: معرفة صحة السمع مرقوفة على العلم بكونه تعالى عالما بجميع المعلومات ، بل الطريق إليه ليس إلا الدليل العقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An exquisitely ordered act proves its maker's knowledge; God's varied, carefully joined bodily structures in the womb also display power to create every possible form.
rows.anchor: الفعل المحكم المتقن يدل على كون فاعله عالما ، فلما كان دليل كونه تعالى عالما هو ما ذكرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The womb's complex, harmonious body formed from a drop is evidence of both omnipotence and knowledge, confirming that God is the Sustainer of all created and possible things.
rows.anchor: قدر أن يخلق من قطرة من النطفة هذه الأعضاء المختلفة في الطبائع والشكل واللون

rows.speaker: النصارى
rows.claim: Christians argued from Jesus' disclosures of private, unseen events that he possessed divine knowledge.
rows.anchor: عيسى عليه السلام كان يخبر عن الغيوب ، وكان يقول لهذا : أنت أكلت في دارك كذا

rows.speaker: النصارى
rows.claim: Christians also cited Jesus' raising the dead, healing the blind and leprous, and making a bird from clay by God's permission as proof of divine power.
rows.anchor: كان يحيي الموتى ، ويبرىء الأكمه والأبرص ، ويخلق من الطين كهيئة الطير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that Jesus knew some hidden matters does not establish divinity, since God could have taught him those facts by revelation.
rows.anchor: لا يلزم من كونه عالما ببعض المغيبات أن يكون إلاها لاحتمال أنه إنما علم ذلك بوحي من الله إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A god must know all its creation; Jesus' ignorance of some unseen matters therefore decisively shows he was not divine.
rows.anchor: عدم إحاطته ببعض المغيبات يدل دلالة قاطعة على أنه ليس بإلاه لأن الإلاه هو الذي لا يخفى عليه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues that if Jesus knew all the unseen, he would have foreknown his captors' plan and the pain of death, and fled before they reached him.
rows.anchor: لو كان عالما بالغيب كله ، لعلم أن القوم يريدون أخذه وقتله ، وأنه يتأذى بذلك ويتألم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing some unseen things cannot prove divinity, whereas ignorance of even some unseen knowledge rules it out.
rows.anchor: الاستدلال بمعرفة بعض الغيب لا يدل على حصول الإلاهية ، وأما الجهل ببعض الغيب يدل قطعا على عدم الإلاهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus' miracles of life and healing in some cases could have been granted by God as honor and proof of his prophethood; they do not establish divinity.
rows.anchor: لا يدل على كونه إلاها ، لاحتمال أن الله تعالى أكرمه بذلك الإحياء إظهارا لمعجزته وإكراما له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A god must be able to create the intricate human form in the womb; Jesus could not do so, so his inability to give or take life at will disproves divinity.
rows.anchor: الإلاه هو الذي يكون قادرا على أن يصور في الأرحام من قطرة صغيرة من النطفة هذا التركيب العجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had Jesus possessed the power to give or take life at will, he could have killed those who seized him, contrary to the Christian account.
rows.anchor: ولو قدر على ذلك لأمات أولئك الذين أخذوه على زعم النصارى وقتلوه

rows.speaker: النصارى
rows.claim: Christians argued that because Jesus had no human father, he must be God's son.
rows.anchor: أن النصارى يقولون : أيها المسلمون أنتم توافقوننا على أنه ما كان له أب من البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ability to form as he wills answers the no-human-father argument: he may create through a father's seed or directly without one.
rows.anchor: فإن شاء صوره من نطفة الأب وإن شاء صوره ابتداء من غير الأب

rows.speaker: النصارى
rows.claim: Christians used the Quranic descriptions of Jesus as God's spirit and word to argue that he is God's son.
rows.anchor: ألست تقول : إن عيسى روح الله وكلمته ، فهذا يدل على أنه ابن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Jesus God's spirit and word is a verbal argument: such expressions may be literal or figurative, and an apparent literal sense that conflicts with reason belongs to the ambiguous verses and must be interpreted by clear verses.
rows.anchor: اللفظ محتمل للحقيقة والمجاز ، فإذا ورد اللفظ بحيث يكون ظاهره مخالفا للدليل العقلي كان من باب المتشابهات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi maps the passage's answers: God's unity and life exclude Christ's divinity and sonship; universal knowledge and the womb's creative power rebut the Christians' knowledge and power arguments.
rows.anchor: قوله { الحى القيوم } إشارة إلى ما يدل على أن المسيح ليس بإلاه ولا ابن له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The titles Mighty and Wise indicate perfect power and knowledge; Christ's partial knowledge and life-giving acts cannot make him divine, since a god must possess both completely.
rows.anchor: فالعزيز إشارة إلى كمال القدرة والحكيم إشارة إلى كمال العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi explicates the statement that nothing is hidden from God as meaning that no thing is hidden from him.
rows.anchor: فالمراد أنه لا يخفى عليه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the warnings and descriptions of opponents in 3:23–25, the command to pray and glorify God distinguishes the Prophet and his followers from the hostile disbelievers.
rows.anchor: أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بدعاء وتمجيد يدل على مباينة طريقه وطريق أتباعه

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil explains اللهم as يا الله, with the doubled mīm replacing the vocative particle يا.
rows.anchor: فقال الخليل وسيبويه { اللهم } معناه : يا الله ، والميم المشددة عوض من : يا

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh shares al-Khalil's derivation of اللهم as يا الله with mīm substituted for يا.
rows.anchor: فقال الخليل وسيبويه { اللهم } معناه : يا الله ، والميم المشددة عوض من : يا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra derives اللهم from يا الله أم بخير, with يا and the hamza of أم dropped through frequent use, comparing it to هلم from هل plus أم.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : كان أصلها ، يا الله أم بخير : فلما كثر في الكلام حذفوا حرف النداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Basran objection is that al-Farra's derivation would require اللهم افعل to take a conjunction before the following request, but speakers do not use one.
rows.anchor: لو كان الأمر على ما قاله الفراء لما صح أن يقال : اللهم افعل كذا إلا بحرف العطف

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra answers that without a conjunction, اغفر لنا explains أمنا, keeping the request to one thing and making the expression more emphatic.
rows.anchor: إذا حذفنا العطف صار قوله : اغفر لنا تفسيرا لقوله : أمنا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj objects that al-Farra's derivation should preserve the original form الله إما, just as an original form can be spoken in ويل أمه.
rows.anchor: حجة الزجاج أنه لو كان الأمر كما قال ، لجاز أن يتكلم به على أصله

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra replies that the alleged original يا الله أمنا is not forbidden, while noting that derived forms need not always be replaceable by their origins; the exclamative ما أكرمه is not used in its supposed base form.
rows.anchor: كثيرا من الألفاظ لا يجوز فيها إقامة الفرع مقام الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Basran objection is that if يا were deleted, يا اللهم should also be allowed, although it is not attested in ordinary use.
rows.anchor: لو كان الأمر على ما قاله الفراء لكان حرف النداء محذوفا ، فكان يجوز أن يقال : يا اللهم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra challenges the assertion that يا اللهم is impossible and introduces a poetic citation to support it.
rows.anchor: فمن الذي سلم لكم أنه لا يجوز أن يقال : يا اللهم وأنشد الفراء

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra cites a poem using يا اللهما after an ordinary vocative; the Basrans call the verse unknown, which Razi says amounts to rejecting transmission and would expose all Arabic to doubt.
rows.anchor: سبحت أو صليت يا اللهما

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra answers that the vocative particle can be omitted, as in يوسف أيها الصديق, so its omission could be specific to this name.
rows.anchor: قد يحذف حرف النداء كقوله { يوسف أيها الصديق أفتنا }

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra argues that if mīm stands for the vocative particle, the address would follow the noun, an impossible order comparable to saying الله يا.
rows.anchor: لكنا قد أخرنا النداء عن ذكر المنادى ، وهذا غير جائز ألبتة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He argues that treating mīm as a replacement for يا should permit the same ending on other names, such as زيدم and بكرم, which Arabic does not allow.
rows.anchor: لو كان هذا الحرف قائما مقام النداء لجاز مثله في سائر الأسماء

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He argues that a replacement for the vocative should not co-occur with يا, but the cited poem contains both.
rows.anchor: لو كان الميم بدلا عن حرف النداء لما اجتمعا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He argues that Arabic has no general pattern of adding mīm to complete nouns to convey a separate particle, so this derivation violates linguistic induction.
rows.anchor: لم نجد العرب يزيدون هذه المييم في الأسماء التامة لإفادة معنى بعض الحروف

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh construes مالك as an accusative vocative, as in قل اللهم فاطر السماوات; it cannot modify اللهم because اللهم combines a noun and a particle.
rows.anchor: قول سيبويه أنه منصوب على النداء ، وكذلك قوله

rows.speaker: المبرد والزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjaj construe مالك as an adjective describing the singular addressee, since اللهم with mīm is equivalent to يا الله and can take an adjective.
rows.anchor: قول المبرد والزجاج أن { مالك } وصف للمنادى المفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported occasion says the Prophet promised his community Persian and Roman rule after the conquest of Mecca; hypocrites and Jews mocked the prospect, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين افتتح مكة وعد أمته ملك فارس والروم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second report places the occasion during the Battle of the Trench: after a huge rock resisted tools, the Prophet broke it with three strikes whose flashes revealed the palaces of Hira, Roman lands, and Sana'a; Gabriel promised victory over them.
rows.anchor: لما خط الخندق عام الأحزاب ، وقطع لكل عشرة أربعين ذراعا ، وأخذوا يحفرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the trench report, hypocrites derided the prophecy because Muslims were too frightened to leave their trench; Razi says the verse was then revealed, while qualifying the account with والله أعلم.
rows.anchor: فقال المنافقون : ألا تعجبون من نبيكم يعدكم الباطل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says God told the Prophet to ask for Persia and Rome and to restore Arab humiliation over them; the command shows the prayer will be answered, as prophets' commanded prayers are answered.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن إن الله تعالى أمر نبيه أن يسأله أن يعطيه ملك فارس والروم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says al-mulk means power and malik means one who is able; God empowers every capable being and grants each owner control of what he owns.
rows.anchor: وقال الملك } هو القدرة ، والمالك هو القادر

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The author of al-Kashshaf instead glosses مالك الملك as owning the entire domain of kingship and disposing of it as owners dispose of their possessions.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) { مالك الملك } أي يملك جنس الملك فيتصرف فيه تصرف الملاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes the kingdom God gives and removes to mean prophethood and messengership, which the Quran calls a great kingdom given to Abraham's family.
rows.anchor: المراد منه : ملك النبوة والرسالة ، كما قال تعالى : { فقد ءاتينا ءال إبراهيم الكتاب والحكمة وءاتيناهم ملكا عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophethood is the greatest kingship: scholars govern inward belief, rulers govern outward affairs, and prophets' authority extends to both belief and practice, including sanctions for rebellion.
rows.anchor: الأنبياء أمرهم نافذ في البواطن والظواهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some rejected human messengers, asking whether God would send a human; the Quran answers that even if God sent an angel, he would appear as a man.
rows.anchor: أبعث الله بشرا رسولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other opponents objected that Muhammad was a poor orphan rather than a notable man from one of the two towns, while Jews insisted prophethood belonged to their ancestors and hypocrites envied his favor.
rows.anchor: إن محمدا فقير يتيم ، فكيف يليق به هذا المنصب العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi recalls that Jews boasted of their numbers, arms, and strength against the Prophet; God answers all such groups by declaring himself owner of sovereignty, who gives it to whom he wills.
rows.anchor: أن اليهود تكبروا على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بكثرة عددهم وسلاحهم وشدتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection to interpreting kingdom as prophethood is that taking it away would mean God deposes a prophet, which cannot happen.
rows.anchor: وجب أن تحملوا قوله { وتنزع الملك ممن تشاء } على أنه قد يعزل عن النبوة من جعله نبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that when God transfers prophethood from an Israelite line to someone outside it, it can be described as removing the kingdom from that line; this answers Jews who treated prophecy as Israel's hereditary right.
rows.anchor: صح أن يقال : إنه ينزع ملك النبوة من بني إسرائيل إلى العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, taking a kingdom can mean withholding it rather than revoking a grant, as with God's bringing people out of darkness and prophets' conditional reply to calls to return to a faith they never held.
rows.anchor: أي تحرمهم ولا تعطيهم هذا الملك لا على معنى أنه يسلبه ذلك بعد أن أعطاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes kingdom in its ordinary worldly sense: wealth and property, public standing and deference, and enforceable command backed by power to defeat rivals.
rows.anchor: عبارة عن مجموع أشياء أحدها : تكثير المال والجاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone distributes worldly wealth and prestige: diligent, clever people may remain poor while heedless people become rich, and rulers may buy public regard without gaining it while others command respect without wealth.
rows.anchor: نرى جمعا في غاية الكياسة لا يحصل لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obedience and victory also come from God; the fact that a small group can overcome a large one by God's leave rationally confirms that he gives kingdom as stated.
rows.anchor: فكم شاهدنا من فئة قليلة غلبت فئة كثيرة بإذن الله ، وعند هذا يظهر بالبرهان العقلي صحة ما ذكره الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Ka'bi says God grants rule by merit and removes it only from someone who sins; he cites the rule that God's covenant does not reach wrongdoers and that knowledge and stature qualified Saul.
rows.anchor: قال الكعبي قوله { تؤتى الملك من تشاء وتنزع الملك ممن تشاء } ليس على سبيل المختارية

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i restricts divinely granted kingship to just rulers: unjust seizure is prohibited, just as prohibited property is excluded from God's provision.
rows.anchor: وقال الجبائي : هذا الحكم مختص بملوك العدل ، فأما ملوك الظلم فلا يجوز أن يكون ملكهم بإيتاء الله

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says removal differs from granting: God can remove rule from just kings for a reason or from unjust kings through death, loss of faculties, destruction of wealth, or by empowering a rightful claimant to depose a usurper; Persian rule was removed by the Messenger in this way.
rows.anchor: ونزع الملك يكون بوجوه : منها بالموت ، وإزالة العقل ، وإزالة القوى ، والقدر والحواس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues an unjust ruler's power either arose without a cause, which denies the Creator, or through divine causes; since people desire rule but cannot all obtain it, tyrants' rule too must be granted by God.
rows.anchor: الأول : نفي للصانع والثاني : باطل لأن كل أحد يريد تحصيل الملك والدولة لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between rulers who naturally inspire awe and success and those who do not shows, on reflection, that rulers' fortunes depend on God's decree.
rows.anchor: ليس إلا بتقدير الله تعالى
